chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya narrated from Salmah ibn al-Khattab from Sulayman ibn Sama'ah al-Khuza'i from Ali ibn Isma'il from 'Amr ibn Abi al-Miqdam who said:

I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying: 'Do you know what is the meaning of the words of Allah, the Exalted: “...that they must not disobey you in lawful matters”?' I said: 'No.' He said: 'Indeed, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said to Fatimah (peace be upon her): “When I die, do not cause abrasion to any face, do not spread for me any hairs, do not cry ‘woe is me,’ and do not call any gathering to mourn for me.” He then said: “This is the lawful matter about which Allah, the Mighty and Glorious, has spoken.”'
ai.seo_question: What does the Quranic phrase 'fi ma'ruf' refer to in the context of Prophet Muhammad's instructions to Fatimah?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi elucidates the Quranic term 'ma'ruf' (customary good conduct) by linking it to the Prophet’s specific instructions to Fatimah (SA) regarding restrained mourning, thereby distinguishing cultural norms of grief from excessive wailing. It highlights the Shia scholarly view that 'ma'ruf' encompasses both divine commandments and established social customs, using the Prophet’s guidance to his daughter as the definitive example of lawful bereavement etiquette.

en.sarwar: 4. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Salmah ibn al-Khattab from Sulayman ibn Sama‘ah al-Khuza‘iy from Ali ibn ‘Isma’il from ‘Amr ibn abu al-Miqdam who has said the following:

“I once heard abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, saying, ‘Do you know what is the meaning of the words of Allah, ‘. . . that they must not disobey you in lawful matters?’ [60:13] I replied, ‘No, I do not know.’ He (the Imam) said, ‘The Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, once said to Fatimah, ‘Alayha al-Salam, ‘When I die, you must not cause abrasion to any face, you must not spread for me any hairs, you must not cry ‘woe is me’ and you must not call any gathering to mourn for me.’ He (the Imam) then said, ‘This is the lawful matter about which Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, has spoken.’”
